title: Minimal Disruption: Runtime & API Rollout Cheat Sheet
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Short cheat-sheet for minimal-disruption runtime + control-plane rollouts in private (VPC/on-prem) customers.
- Focus: safe staged upgrades, lightweight API compatibility checks, terraform notes for module changes, and immediate rollback triggers.
- Intended audience: SRE on-call, release engineer, customer success lead during upgrade windows.

Assumptions:
- Customer has Dedicated or Private control plane with standard TF modules applied.
- Pre-upgrade backup snapshots and state backups are available.
- We have a verified smoke-suite for that customer (prompt tests + routing tests).

Preflight checklist (do before any change):
1) Verify backups: TF state, DB snapshots, KV store backup times, and file system snapshots. Confirm recovery steps documented.
2) Validate service-level feature flags are off for experimental features.
3) Confirm capacity headroom: at least 30% buffer on GPU pool and control-plane replicas for surge.
4) Security: ensure KMS/HSM keys available in target region and rotated credentials for deploy bot.
5) Linked tickets: confirm DEPLOY-412 and a temporary escalation Slack channel is open.
6) Customer communication: send upgrade window + expected blast radius and rollback window.

Staged rollout plan (recommendation, 45-90 minute window depending on scope):
- Phase 0: Dry run on staging mirror (run full smoke-suite). Duration: 15-30m.
- Phase 1: Canary wave (1-2 hosts or 1% traffic) using blue instances with new runtime. Run targeted smoke-suite and lightweight throughput test. Duration: 10-15m.
- Phase 2: Incremental waves (25%, 50%, 100%) with monitoring checks between waves. Use traffic mirroring if possible. Typical pause 10-15m between waves.
- Phase 3: Control plane rollout last. Only after runtime waves are stable for 30m.
- Phase 4: Post-upgrade regressions run and confirm metrics for 1 hour.

Key automated checks between waves (fail-fast triggers):
- Error rate > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5m => automatic pause and alert.
- Latency P95 increase > 30% over baseline spike for 5m => pause.
- Token generation failure/retry rate > 1% => rollback.
- Model output regression alerts triggered by eval harness for canary prompts => rollback.

API compatibility checklist (quick):
- Confirm API schema version header compatibility: new runtime must accept previous version headers.
- Input validation: missing fields should default to prior behavior.
- Response envelope: do not add required fields to top-level response. Keep additions behind 'extensions' field.
- Function/tool-calling hooks: if changed ABI, provide shim that maps older tool names.
- Streaming protocol: maintain same chunk boundaries and sentinel tokens.
- Backwards compatibility tests: run 50 legacy client prompts against canary and compare hashes for structural changes (allow non-determinism tolerance).

Terraform module notes and quick tips:
- State migration: if module names change, use terraform state mv to rehome resources before plan/apply. Example: terraform state mv module.old_name.aws_instance.foo module.new_name.aws_instance.foo
- Provider pinning: pin provider versions in lockfile to avoid accidental provider upgrades during rollout.
- Immutable infra signals: prefer creating new instances and switching traffic vs in-place edits for runtime binaries.
- Module versioning: publish a small semver change for infra-only tweaks (0.x -> 0.x+1) and reference exact module version in customer configs for the window.
- drift check: run terraform plan with -detailed-exitcode and fail the rollout if unexpected diffs found.

Rollback patterns and commands (fast paths):
- Fast revert to prior runtime image: trigger traffic switch in the router/orchestration layer (example: kubectl set image or terraform apply to previous ASG launch config).
- Control plane fallback: if control plane API regression detected, redirect agents to read-only control plane and re-enable older control plane if warm replicas exist.
- DB migration rollbacks: avoid destructive forward-only migrations during this window. If happened, follow DB runbook.
- Example quick commands (customer-managed k8s):
  - kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deploy/rw-runtime --to-revision=3
  - terraform apply -var=oci_image_tag=previous-tag modules/compute
  - curl -fS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://canary.example.local/health || echo 'canary failed'

Smoke-suite and test prompts (minimal set):
- Health checks: /health, /metrics, /ready endpoints.
- Prompt tests: 20 short prompts (intent detection), 10 long-context prompts (>1024 tokens) to exercise KV cache and longer attention.
- Streaming test: start streaming call and verify chunk sequence and final sentinel.
- Tool calling: one prompt exercising tool call + callback roundtrip.
- Embeddings regression: 5 embeddings vectors compared with cosine similarity threshold >= 0.995 for non-quantized models; for quantized models lower threshold allowed.

Metrics to watch during rollout (dashboards):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for generation and single-turn.
- Token/sec throughput across cluster.
- Model GPU utilization and memory OOM events.
- Control plane API 5xx/4xx split.
- Cache hit ratio for KV/prefix cache.
- Cost estimate delta per 1M tokens.

Communication and runbook roles (one-line responsibilities):
- Release lead: coordinates waves and pauses.
- SRE on-call: monitors infra metrics and initiates rollback triggers.
- Runtime engineer: available for hotfixes and binary rollbacks.
- CS lead: customer liaison and status updates.

Post-upgrade actions (first 24 hours):
- Run full regression harness overnight.
- Hold a 60m postmortem within 24 hours if any automated trigger fired.
- If stable for 24h, schedule module cleanup and state pruning.

Common gotchas and tips (war stories):
- Shims are lifesavers: small compatibility shims in API surface can buy time when downstream clients lag.
- Don’t change binary serialization layout and expect clients to cope.
- Large batch size defaults can hide perf regressions; test with production-like batches.
- Quantization changes can shift embedding distributions; keep separate evaluations for embeddings-heavy customers.

Quick escalation script (copy-paste for Slack):
- \"UPGRADE ALERT: customer X, stage canary failed. Error rate up. Paging SRE, runtime eng, and CS. See DEPLOY-412. Rolling back to previous runtime as of 14:32 UTC.\"

Notes for follow-up docs (todo):
- Add terraform state migration cookbook with exact commands per module.
- Build an automated canary harness for API backwards-compat checks.
- Add a templated customer communication email for visible scheduled maintenance.
